page: Amazon Web Services m6g.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, exposing 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local NVMe storage and no hardware accelerators, depending on remote network storage for disk operations while delivering a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight clear architectural tradeoffs between single-thread execution speeds and multi-core parallel capacity. Single-threaded tasks demonstrate constrained execution, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 932.0 and gzip compression throughput of 19.93 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-threaded workloads leverage the 32 dedicated physical cores effectively, achieving a stress-ng multi-core result of 47614.83, a Geekbench multi-core score of 11362.0, and Clang compilation benchmark of 25659.0. Memory bandwidth scales to 158.2 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 75.53 GB/sec for large block writes, though PassMark overall memory scoring remains lower at 1812.35.

From an infrastructure perspective, m6g.8xlarge delivers predictable parallel throughput and resource isolation free from hyperthreading contention. Benchmark results show consistent execution in data services, registering 35.96 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 20248.68 in PassMark database operations, accompanied by 32.42 GB/sec in static web serving. The balanced resource distribution makes m6g.8xlarge appropriate for containerized web microservices, relational databases, distributed in-memory caches, continuous integration build nodes, and general backend application serving.

128.0 GB system RAM providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio
